mainEntity.name: Do I need to prime after surface preparation, or can I skip it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Priming after surface preparation is generally recommended and rarely advisable to skip. Primer creates a consistent base for the topcoat, improving paint adhesion, hiding minor imperfections, and sealing porous surfaces. It also helps block stains and ensures a more uniform color. Skipping primer can lead to uneven paint absorption, poor adhesion, and a less durable finish, especially when painting over bare materials or significant color changes.
acceptedAnswer.description: Priming after surface preparation is almost always recommended to improve paint adhesion, seal surfaces, hide imperfections, and ensure a durable, uniform finish.
